# dsh-ui-colors
> Customize maximum theme coverage with a minimal set of controls.
This is a UI plugin I wrote for myself for controlling how DSH WEB client looks like. Basically I wa
nted to achieve maximum theme coverage with a small set of controls. I mainly use DSH from VS Code,
where I already have a custom editor theme, so I wanted to match built-in browser `dsh web` window w
e a custom editor theme, so I wanted to match built-in browser `dsh web` window with my IDE's theme.
Directly applying VS Code theme into DSH is not possible without some crude adapters, so instead I s
tarted with dsh-web-ui-design-spec.md and built this plugin. It modifies basic primitives and color
tokens, so UI should be consistent in other plugins that utilize the same default DSH CSS. Yes, of c
ourse you can modify the UI, using the agent itself, but here's the plugin already that covers most
of basic UI needs for majority of geeks out there.
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/38989c9b-eb91-4b53-b662-8c608da9e6c2

## What this UI plugin offers and adds in DSH?
Under **Settings → Customize**:

- **Palette** — nine spectra, color presets, and the **Full semantic theme** switch.
- **Syntax high

lighter** — six Shiki token themes: Default, GitHub, Nord, Dracula, Solarized, Monokai.
- **Selectio

n** — **Apply spectrum to ::selection**, independent of the full theme.
- **Colors / Neutral / Borde

rs** — per-surface fills, 16 neutral steps, and four border colors.
- **Border radius** — Default, H

alf, or None.
- **Language** — English and Simplified Chinese follow the DSH locale setting; changin
g the DSH language updates the section without a reload.
The `dsh-ui-colors` plugin adds a "Customize" section under "Settings", where you can have some opti
ons to tweak: under Palette you have a "Spectrum" to choose from main accent colors, and under "Pres
et" there are some basic presets that change the values of surface fills, neutral color steps and bo
e some basic presets that change the values of surface fills, neutral color steps and border colors.
You also have a "Full semantic theme" switch, where the colors from the spectrum are also applied wi
th its own inner color scope, adding some more colors instead of just hue and saturation from one ma
n inner color scope, adding some more colors instead of just hue and saturation from one main color.
For those who are paying meticulous attention to details, the `::selection` of the text can also be
overriden by checking independent option "Apply spectrum to ::selection". Also "Border radius" can b
e changed from default to half and to none (having square, sharp corners if someone prefers).
DSH uses the Shiki syntax highlighter, so that colors can be changed too. There are already a few th
e Shiki syntax highlighter, so that colors can be changed too. There are already a few themes added.
If customization is needed, you can always add your "Spectrum" colors or "Presets". The data lives i
n `lib/client.js` and adding a spectrum or preset is a small source change. The agent can help with
b/client.js` and adding a spectrum or preset is a small source change. The agent can help with that.
Oh, and of course you can manually modify some values per surface in "Colors", also changing some "N
eutral" values here and there and to play around with "Borders".

## Caveats
- **Main**, **Right panel**, and **Sidebar** attach their scoped rules through CSS-module suffixes (
`*_centerCol`, `*_rightbarCol`, `*_sidebarCol`). If a future DSH build renames one, that surface's b
ackground token or override still applies, but its scoped container styling falls back to the theme.
- Only the sidebar auto-adjusts text. Main, composer, panel, bubble, and code fills keep the theme'

s text colors, so very dark fills in light mode (or the reverse) can reduce readability.
- Menus use
a translucent material (`--dsw-specific-menu`); overriding it with an opaque color is intentionally

not exposed.
- The radius preset uses the six values from `base.css` in the installed build. If a f

uture DSH build changes the base radius scale, update `RADIUS_DEFAULTS` in `lib/client.js`.
- Overla
ys that escape a surface (for example, a popover anchored to the Settings button) keep the normal th

eme surface.
- The settings shell has no public per-section icon option, so the pipette is a CSS mas
k applied to the `Customize` nav button after it renders. If the section label is changed, update `S
ECTION_LABEL` and the nav-tagging logic; otherwise the shell falls back to its default settings icon
